ᾤα.definition: = sheepskin, Hermipp.57 , cf; garment of this material, a sort of drawers or apron, used by bathers, Theopomp.Com.37; Pherecr.62; worn at certain sacred rites, Hermipp.53

ᾠδή.definition: contr. for song, lay, ode, h.Ap.20; = magic song, spell, Longus2.7

ὤκινον.definition: a fodder-plant, perhaps clover , Lat. ocinum, Cato RR27,33 , Varro RR1.31

ὠμίασις.definition: shouldering, an allegorization of the name Shechem, Ph.1.92, 471

ὤμιλλα.definition: a game in which nuts, etc., were thrown into a ring : hence metaph. of a party, circle, Eup.250; Id.288

ᾠόν.definition: old poet. forms v. sub fin.:—egg; of the eggs or spawn of fish, Hdt.2.93; Arist.HA567b22, cf. 525a7; of serpents, ib.558a26; of tortoises, ib.558a4

ὡραῖος.definition: produced at the right season; = esp. at their first appearance, Hp.Superf.34

ὤριος.definition: nightly, cj. Brunck in Mesom.Sol.22, where codd., fort. recte

ὡρίτης.definition: ruler of the Seasons, of Apollo, Lyc.352; Anecd.Stud. 267

ὡροτρόφος.definition: fostering the seasons, bringing them on, of the sun, Orph.H.8.10, cf. 38.25

ὠτίον.definition: prop. Dim. of auricle, Dsc.Eup.1.63; metaph., a little handle, HeroSpir.1.9; Theopomp.Com.31, cf. Aët.1.138

ὤχρα.definition: yellow ochre, Arist.Mete.378a23, Thphr.Lap.40; in corn, = mildew, LXXDe.28.22

ὤψ.definition: EM344.55, but Ar.Byz. , Eust.1426.55 , gen. acc. face, countenance, Hom. and Hes., only in acc. sing.; to look one in the face, Il.9.373; 15.147: abs., Od.22.405, cf. 23.107; in face she is like the goddesses, Il.3.15…

ὦ.definition: and an exclamation, expressing surprise, joy, or; with voc., a mode of address, whether at the beginning of a sentence or in a parenthesis, Il.1.74, etc., esp. in dialogue and Oratt., Antipho.5.1; in invocations of th…

ὠβάζω.definition: divide the people into v. foreg

ὠδίνω.definition: used by early writers only in pres.: fut; c. acc., to be in travail of a child, bring forth, E.IA1234, LXXCa.8.5: of animals, Ael.NA2.46: prov., Luc.Hist.Conscr.23

ὠθέω.definition: mostly of human force, as of Sisyphus, he kept pushing it . . , Od.11.596, cf. 599; 22.20; pushed it away from . . , Il.5.854; 1.220; 15.668; ib.694, cf. 13.193; 5.19; ib.835, etc.; so rush into the fire, Hdt.7.167; t…

ὠθίζω.definition: = thrust, push, or push on; Med., push against one another, jostle, struggle, Luc.Pisc.42; Aristid.2.95J., 1.388 J.: metaph., wrangle, Hdt.3.76

ὠΐζω.definition: to sit on eggs, brood, Id

ὠκύαλος.definition: perh. sea-swift, speeding o'er the; later, generally, swift, violent, Opp.H.2.535, cf. Pi.Parth.2.19

ὠκύπος.definition: poet. form of sq., of Apollo, AP9.525.25

ὠκυτοκία.definition: speedy delivery, cj. for in Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.133

ὠκυτόκος.definition: causing quick and easy birth; of a river, giving quick increase, S.OC689

ὠλένιος.definition: in the elbow or arm, the star

ὠμοβόειος.definition: having set before me a slice of raw beef, and mixed me three cups yet more raw than beef, AP11.137

ὠμόδροπος.definition: plucked unripe, prop. the right of plucking the fresh fruit, metaph. for the rights of the marriage-bed, the husband's rights, A.Th.333

ὠμοθετέω.definition: in sacrificing, place the raw pieces duly on the altar, Il.1.461, 2.424, Od.3.458:—Med., 14.427: later, generally, sacrifice, A.R.3.1033 . that some derived it fr. shoulder, and expld. it accordingly.)

ὠμοίδης.definition: with swollen or high shoulders, Eust.1684.28

ὠμόσιτος.definition: eating raw meat, of the Sphinx, eating; Pass., eaten raw, Lyc.654

ὠμοφάγος.definition: eating raw flesh, carnivorous; rarely proparox. Pass., eaten raw, of sacrifices offered to Dionysus, E.Fr.472.12

ὠνητής.definition: buyer, purchaser, X.Oec.2.3; contractor, IG22.1596.3; lessee of mines, ib.1587.4, al

ᾠοβραχής.definition: soaked in white of egg, Leonid. ap. Aët.6.1, Heliod. ap.Orib.48.33.1

ᾠόγαλα.definition: eggs mixed with milk, Paul. Aeg.3.42, 6.8, Aët.9.42, etc

ᾠοειδής.definition: egg-shaped, ovoid, Arist.HA539b12; = the aqueous humour of the eye, Gal.19.358, Aët.7.1

ᾠοθεσία.definition: row of eggs, i.e. ovate border, Aristeas62

ᾠοσκύφιον.definition: egg-shaped cup with a double bottom, Asclep.Myrl. ap. Ath.11.503e, cf. 488f

ᾠοτοκέω.definition: lay eggs, Arist.HA566b1, etc.; opp; of plants, produce seed, Emp.79

ᾠοφόρος.definition: bearing eggs or roe, Arist.HA621b20; the pains of egg-laying, Opp.H.1.478

ᾠοφυλακέω.definition: guard their eggs, of the males of some fish, esp. the Silurus, Arist.HA568b13, 621a23, al

ὡρογενής.definition: in pl., gods who preside over the several hours of the day, PMag.Leid.W.1.30, cf. 9.37

ὡροθετέω.definition: take note of a thing in casting a nativity; to be in the ascendant at the natal hour, of one's ruling planet, ib.161

ὤστης.definition: one who thrusts or pushes; an earthquake with one violent shock, Arist.Mu.396a8

ὠτειλή.definition: wound, esp. a fresh, open wound, Il. (acc; after Hom. generally, wound, whether recent or not, Hp.Art.11; also, the mark of a wound, scar, ibid., cf. Ruf.Ren.Ves.Praef.: ulcer, Gal.19.157:—once in X., add. codd. pleri…

ὠτοειδής.definition: like an ear, ear-shaped, Ruf.Anat.32. Adv. ibid

ὠτολαβίς.definition: an instrument for laying hold of the ears, . . Hippiatr.99

ὠφέλημα.definition: a useful or serviceable thing; things good in themselves, e.g. harmony, goodwill, opp. Stoic.3.23, cf.136

ὠφελητέος.definition: proper to be served; one must serve, ib.2.1.28

ὠχραίνω.definition: make pale or wan, Orph.A.1308:—Pass., to; intrans., to be or become so, Nic.Th.254

ὠχράω.definition: turn pale or wan, Od.11.529; of the sun, Arat.851

ὠχρίας.definition: one of a pale complexion, Arist.Cat.9b32

ὠαιαί.definition: exclam. of pain, A.D.Adv.127.31; also Aeol. for ib.128.2, cf. Theoc.30.1, Lex.Mess.p.412

ὧδε.definition: Att. also , demonstr.Adv. of; of Manner, in this wise, thus, sts. so very, so exceedingly, freq. from Hom. downwards: in Hom. usu. before the Verb, but after it in Il.1.181, 574, 10.91, 18.392; Pl. and X. mostly place…

ὦκα.definition: poet. Adv. of quickly, swiftly, Il.1.402; of Time, immediately, Od.17.329, Il.18.527, al.:—Cleitorian word acc. to AB1096

ὡσαύτως.definition: Adv. of in like manner, just so, used; further strengthd., so in like manner, Pl.Grg.460d; Id.Phd.78d

ὡσεί.definition: or Adv. as if, as though; with various; with Numerals, or measures of time and space, about, Hdt.7.109, cf. X.HG1.2.9, LXXGe.24.55, al., Ev.Matt.14.21, al

ὥσπερ.definition: or Adv. of Manner, like as, even as; c. subj., v. infr.III; c. opt., . . Pl.Phd.87b, cf. X.HG3.1.14; cf. II

ὠτειλῆθεν.definition: Adv. from or out of the wound, Orph.L.653

ὠμοτριβής.definition: pressed raw, oil from unripe olives, preferred for many purposes, Thphr.Od.15, Dsc.1.30

ὠκυφόνος.definition: quickly fatal, of diseases, prob. in Aret.SA2.3

ὠφέλησις.definition: helping, aiding, hence, like use, service, advantage, S.OC401; Id.El.1031

ὡρονόμος.definition: hour-divider, i.e. a dial or; in Astrology, = II.1, ascendant, Man.1.30, 262, 3.120, Doroth. ap. Heph. Astr.2.24

ὠτότμητος.definition: with ears slit or cropped, LXXLe.21.18, 22.23

ὡροδρόμημα.definition: space traversed in an hour, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.23

ὡροκράτωρ.definition: the lord of the hour, Ps.-Ptol.Centil.90

ὡρολόγος.definition: an Egyptian astrologer, Chaerem. ap. Porph.Abst.4.8

ὠνητέος.definition: to be bought, Pl.Lg.849c, Amphis1.4; one must buy, Luc.Herm.58

ὠκυπόδης.definition: poet. for AP5.222 ; 9.371: in Dor. form, E.Hyps.Fr.1 ii 34

ὡρόμαντις.definition: the hour-prophet, of the cock, prob. in Babr.124.15

ὠμότης.definition: rawness, crudeness, opp; indigestion, crudity, Thphr.Lass.4, D.S.10.7: pl., Plu.2.661b, cf. Dsc.3.1

ὠμοτοκέω.definition: bring forth untimely, miscarry, LXXJb.21.10; . . D.H.9.40

ὠμογέρων.definition: a fresh, active old man; one untimely old, as expl. of the Ep. , EM821.48: so as Adj., AP5.263

ὠκυπορέω.definition: move quickly, Str.8.3.29; of a ship, Epigr.Gr.981.10

ὥριος.definition: generally, in due season, seasonable, Hes.Op.392, 422; ib.697; Opp. l.c., cf. AP9.311 ; ib.10.100 ; Arat.154; c. inf., it is time . . , Sol.27.9

ὠμοκυδιάω.definition: to be proud of broad shoulders, Com.Adesp.1201

ὥρασι.definition: Adv.: ):—in season, in good time, as an imprecation, may he not come in season, i.e. bad luck to him! Alex.266.1, Luc.DMeretr.10.3; . . Men.Pk.131; Ar.Lys.1037 ; that fellow—bad luck to him! ib.391; . . Luc.Salt.5; al…

ὠνησείω.definition: Desiderat. of wish to buy, D.C.47.14

ὠμηστής.definition: Dor. eating raw; savage, brutal, Il.24.207, cf. Plu.Ant.24

ὡρολογητής.definition: one that tells of the , of Prodicus, who composed a speech entitled Timo18, cf. Eust.1349.10

ὠμαμπέλινος.definition: of the colour of the fresh vine- leaf, opp. Peripl.M.Rubr.65

ὠκυλόχεια.definition: giving a quick birth, of Artemis, Orph.H.2.4, 36.8; of ib.10.19

ὠμοτομέω.definition: cut an abscess before it is ripe or fully purulent, Paul. Aeg.6.34:—hence Archig. ap. Gal.12.677

ὦσις.definition: = thrusting, pushing, Hp.Aph.3.26 ; opp. Arist.Ph.243a17, de An.433b25; of an injury to the skull, depression, Gal. ap. Orib.46.21.1: pl., thrusts, Plu.2.916d, Procl.in Ti.1.297 D., al

ὥ.definition: Dor. for A.D.Pron.48.27, Synt.156.22, al; Dor. for Leg.Gort.10.36, SIG47.21 , Theoc.3.11, al.; . . shd. be read in IG4.823.66, cf. 33 : formed like Dor. =

ὠμία.definition: shoulder, i.e. angle, of a building, LXX3 Ki.6.13, 7.17, al., cf. PVat.11rv16

ὠλεσίοικος.definition: destroying the house, (sc; squandering one's substance, Com.Adesp.1200

ὡρόδεσμος.definition: straw rope for binding sheaves, Eust.1162.32

ὠκύροος.definition: poet. Adj. swift-flowing, Il.5.598, 7.133:—fem. an Oceanid, h.Cer.420, Hes.Th.360

ὠκιμοειδής.definition: like neut. as Adv; catchfly, Silene gallica, Dsc.4.28, Gal.12.158

ὠρυθμός.definition: a howling, of dogs, Opp.C.4.219 ; of a lion, roaring, Theoc.25.217

ὡριόκαρπος.definition: with ripe or timely fruit, Orph.H.56.11

ὠμόϋπνος.definition: with one's sleep not slept out, Eup.305; Philostr.VA8.31

ὡρομέδων.definition: ruling the seasons, of Phoebus, IG12.893 , Epigr.Gr.1036.2

ὡροσκόπος.definition: Astrol., caster of nativities; Adj., of the ascendant , Man.4.59, cf. 496

ὠμοτόκος.definition: bringing forth immature offspring, Call.Cer.53; Id.Del.120 : metaph. of a vine, AP9.561

ὠρεσίδουπος.definition: poet. for making a din on the mountains, AP9.524.25

ὠχρίασις.definition: a turning pale, paleness, Sor.1.45; = II, Thd.Am. 4.9

ὠτόρρυτος.definition: having a running from the ears, Hp.Epid.6.1.2

ὠμόλινον.definition: raw flax, A.Fr.206; used for lint; coarse linen towel or napkin, Cratin.9 , Plu.2.509a

ὤνιος.definition: Aeschin.3.160; also Luc.Nigr.25; of a venal magistrate, Din.1.20; Arist.Pol.1270b10; so Plu.Cat.Mi.21

ὡς.definition: come, che, affinché, quando; + participio = valore causale/finale soggettivo; + superlativo = il più possibile (ὡς τάχιστα); + acc. = verso (persone)
